description:
Owner decision needed: how should the nightly DuckDB performance gate judge the aggregate metrics (Total Execution Time and Average Query Time), given that the 10% aggregate check fails on host noise? Options:
(a) Keep 10%. t3:perf stays red most nights.
(b) Raise the aggregate threshold to 15%. Simple, but the same-class spread is wide enough that it would still fail on bad nights.
(c) Add an absolute floor to the aggregate check: fail only when the aggregate is both more than 10% slower and more than N ms slower, with N taken from the same-class spread (about 65 ms). Needs a change in benchbox/cli/commands/compare.py, because --min-regression-delta applies to per-query checks only (compare.py:284: "Aggregate metrics are judged by percentage alone").
(d) Make aggregates report-only and keep the per-query gate.
(e) Judge against rolling same-runner-class history, or require two consecutive red nights before failing.
(f) Increase the signal (more iterations or a larger scale factor), or gate run wall time instead.
Recommendation: (c) or (e).

Evidence:
- The aggregate is the sum of the same 66 per-query timings (22 queries x 3 iterations, about 8 ms each) that the per-query check already judges. It adds no independent signal.
- In run 37991400931 all 22 queries slowed together (+2.7% to +45.8%) on the baseline's own runner class (AMD EPYC 7763). That pattern is host noise, not a code regression.
- Same-class aggregate totals so far: 539.8, 542.9, 546.4, 548.9, 586.1 and 604.7 ms. One night in six already exceeds 10% over the lowest.
- The gate does not measure orchestration overhead: run.total_duration_ms is not compared.
- perf-smoke.yml runs only on pull requests to the release branch (perf-smoke.yml:3-5), so the "Per-PR" title and wording in docs/development/perf-smoke.md are wrong.
- t3:perf failed in 11 of the last 12 nightly-v2 runs.

Context: the refreshed EPYC 7763 baseline still produced a +10.47% aggregate result in nightly-v2 run 37991400931 while every per-query regression stayed within the 7 ms floor.
